sentences.text: Heard Sri. S.M. Faisal Warsi, Sri. Raj Kumar Awasthi, Sri. Fayzan khan learned counsel for the applicants, learned counsel for the opposite party as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.

This anticipatory bail application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in Complaint Case No.
118 of 2021 (Special Session Trial No. 391 of 2022) under Sections 376-D, 504, 506 I.P.C. and 5, 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012 and Section 67 of the Information Technology Act, 2000, Police Station Puranderpur, District Maharajganj.

sentences.text: It is submitted that in this case applicants are innocent and have committed no offence but on account of civil litigation between both the parties present complaint was filed before the Special Judge POCSO Act by the mother of the victim with false allegations of entering fingers in the private part of the victim by grabbing her mouth.
Video was also prepared with mobile phone.
The household items were also damaged.
During this period the victim was alone on the place of occurrence.

Information was given to the police but no F.I.R. was lodged though there is nothing on record to show that information was given to the police or any Superior Authority of Police regarding the aforesaid incident.
It is further submitted that there are 14 civil cases pending before both the parties that was the reason of false implication.

No any inquiry was conducted by the learned court as required under Section 200, 202 Cr.P.C. but only on the basis of statements made by the complainant, victim and other witness related to them summoning order was made without applying the judicial mind and without assessing the material on record.

It is also submitted that medical is said to have got done on the second day of the alleged incident but no any injury was found on the private part of the victim to suggest that the alleged offence was committed with her by the applicants those were several in numbers.
Even complaint of pain was also not made by the victim to the doctor which also infer that no offence in the nature of using finger in the private part of the victim was committed by the applicants.
Since applicants are under apprehension of imminent arrest.
In case, the applicants are released on bail, they would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the trial, so requested for anticipatory bail.

Learned counsel for the opposite party as well as learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid but could not rebut the fact as mentioned in the medical report regarding any injury or complaint of pain in private part of the victim.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for both the parties as well as learned A.G.A., perusal of record, the long drawn litigation between both the parties and medical report there appears ground to grant anticipatory bail in favour of the applicants during the pendency of trial.

The applicants- Akbar, Kutbuddin, Ram Achal, Rampreet and Krishna Mohan, shall be released on anticipatory bail on furnishing a personal bond with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicants shall appear before the learned court everyday when case is fixed except exempted;
(ii) The applicants shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police office;
(iii) The applicants shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court and if they have passport, the same shall be deposited by them before the S.S.P./S.P.
concerned.
